lessons.trap: In the 10-lens deepen, and in the review path the plan sets up, a lens or verifier that crashed or hit a limit returns the same empty shape as a clean pass. Score zero votes as ABSTAIN and read the failures block before folding (the '0 abstained' count is exactly this check).

Folding the deepen's lens findings into the plan: a generative lens never reaches zero findings, so close on finding class rather than count, and check each confirmed prescription against source before folding it in.

Making ultramode-code-review mandatory and choosing the CE review path can silently drop a cadence step, such as the always-on generative adversary or the latest-model reviewers (they once defaulted to sonnet). Re-derive the cadence's value instead of assuming it carries over.

The squeaky-clean peer-session guard is the shared-working-tree problem: other sessions couple through the tree itself (scratch files, a shared git index, EOL flips, half-landed edits). One session's cleanup or commit can delete or sweep up another session's work.

The plan is built from preflight squawks S1–S14, and each one comes with a prescription. A correct diagnosis does not make its fix true. Check that every setting key, hook event or plugin option a prescription names actually exists before it becomes a plan step.

Lens agents running with full tool access during the deepen can leave probe or scratch files in the tree. A confident lens finding about how Claude Code or CE behaves is a hypothesis to check, not a verdict to fold.

A deepen or review workflow script that hands live promises (Array.from mapFn) to parallel() crashes every verifier, and .filter(Boolean) turns that into an empty 'clean' result. Read the failures channel first.
The deepen's lens agents emitting big multi-question StructuredOutput calls get truncated after the first property and die in the retry loop. Cap schema field sizes and array lengths.

A confidence or priority filter in the deepen's or review flow's verify fan-out drops findings into no bin at all. Every finding must end up confirmed, refuted, abstained or unverified, and the entered-versus-exited set difference must be explained.

Making the flow mandatory and cleaning up plugins replaces old process decisions. CLAUDE.md, memory files and skills that cite the old flow are the blast radius, so grep for the old premise phrases, not just the files the plan names.

Plan gates that name concrete external targets (a CE version, a config key, an MCP endpoint, a settings field) must be checked to exist when the gate is written. A 'known blocker' from one failed preflight probe deserves a real recon attempt before it shapes the plan.

A plan written from preflight reports proves coherence, not currency. The CLI and plugins auto-update, so preflight facts about versions, settings and hooks may have drifted by build time. Re-read the live state.

A settings.json env var, permission entry or .compound-engineering/config.yaml key the plan relies on only does something if the harness or plugin actually reads it. Grep for the consumer before claiming the switch works.
Settings have layered scopes (user/project/local/managed). An edit that restates a value another scope already sets, or that a higher scope overrides, is a no-op. Prove the effective value moved.

~/.claude/hooks/*.sh are hand-maintained copies of projects/hooks/, kept in sync only by an 'edit both, cmp' note. A copy with a warning beside it rots anyway: replace it with a pointer (a junction) or wire a gate.

A copy swap on a fold-law frame is really a layout change. Rewording or reordering verdictMedicarePriced/verdictMedicareResidual can wrap one extra line on ubuntu's text metrics and push the R13 disclaimer past the fold while local Windows verify:fit stays green. Size the new sentences by wrap class, and fix by shortening the true referent, not with whitespace surgery.

The priced-Medicare pair (.cs-medicare-residual--typical) already sits at the floor of the one-frame degrade ladder: whitespace, leading and type register are all spent. Growing the residual monolith or the lead text has no rung left, so cutting content or shrinking the hero would break the law. Every computed-style pin must still hold.

Rewording the trim note, the Medicare line and the residual lead updates copy.ts, but prop-docs and comments that quote the old wording or describe the old list order stay false. Grep the OLD words and the old structural claim across src/** including comments, and update every hit.

Edits that move copy.ts strings and the healthcareSheet block shift line numbers under docs that cite verdictMedicarePriced and others by line. The structural gate stays green while the meaning rots. Run doc:reanchor once at the end, then restore insight 136's own record line numbers rather than re-pointing them.

The Medicare affirmation was written for the typical household and misled a household that also lands on it: a $0-premium Medicare Advantage couple read its copays as counted on top. Each reworded sentence must be true for every household its predicate routes there, not just the typical one.

The Healthcare sheet and verdict copy can pass every test and still fail the reader: list far from its subject, unquoted referents, mechanism vocabulary. Apply the microcopy law (quote every referenced quantity, one word per mechanism) and treat the Caddie walk or a cold read as the gate.

verdictResidualLead plus composed parts beside a verdictMedicareResidual monolith is a split-key shape. Rewording one variant without grepping every renderer of the other leaves a live surface telling yesterday's wording.

Fixing how the Medicare line reads on the verdict does not fix sibling surfaces that say the same thing through their own chrome, such as the health sheet's Medicare note or the date route's priced note. Enumerate them from the rendered screen, not by grepping the copy key.

verdictMedicarePriced ('Medicare's premiums for the two of you are already in these numbers') is gated by a producer-output predicate. If the reword widens what it claims is counted (copays, extras), the gate must still read the built overlay's real pricing decision, or the claim renders over runs that never priced it.

Moving the per-person extras block right under the Medicare premium card touches the filed framing fork (the loud figure is Part-B-scoped while extras roughly double the bill) and the provenance-mixed extras (typical placeholder vs entered). The new adjacency must not read as folding extras into the headline. healthSheetSeedGate pins rendered strings that will need re-cutting.

If the reworded frames fail fit only on ubuntu CI (the pending nc arm at bottom=769), a passing local Windows run proves nothing. Any fix must show a measured computed-value delta in the failing regime and must check which density tier already owns the values.

Briggsy's b9-1 rulings arrived as filed prescriptions, and the walk then showed one of them (the Medicare line) misleading a real household, which forced the b9-2 re-ruling. Check each filed wording against the live render and the predicate's households before shipping it as-is.

The §7 clamp keys income-blind (alive && t < retire) while guards keyed on earnedIncomeReal > 0; presence-keying the working-year pricing and the IRMAA lag-read clamped-year override on anything but the clamp's own predicate (accumulation construct present) leaves the zero-wage worker unguarded.

A clamped working year has net draw ≈ 0, which is exactly the slow-convergence regime (small net plus uncapped SS torpedo). Running solveGrossWithdrawal over wages needs its pass count probed at net = 0, not at a big draw that hides the worst case under GROSS_UP_MAX_PASSES.

Stacking wages under the conversion/RMD inside the same gross-up fixed point can open a new high-k corner (wages + torpedo + gain straddle). Re-derive k from the sum of channels and prove the worst corner is still disjoint instead of assuming contraction still holds.

The §86 provisional-base comparison must divide the frozen nominal $32k/$44k lines by cumulativePriceIndex for the sim calendar year (calendarYear is a required arg). The new tax(W+X)−tax(W) call sites must thread it, and a prediction that pins won't move must be measured (record first, then re-tune seeds).

The dip seed's Y=5 crown exists because an absolute-year conversion window collides with retirement-anchored draws while the §7 clamp zeroes work-year withdrawals. Taxing working-year conversions over wages changes that tent, so the crown pins must be re-derived from the mechanism, not assumed to hold.

Reduce-to-spine byte-identity holds only if it is compared per vector. A check on totals passes any reallocation between buckets, and the absent-construct identity needs a moved-witness showing the construct-present run actually changes tax.

Testing clamped years and retired years separately misses the crossing year, where wages stop, the pricing regime switches and the 2-year IRMAA lag first reads a clamped year's MAGI. That year needs its own fixture.

The clamped-year IRMAA override is the entered working-year MAGI, not a salary-derived figure, and earnedIncomeReal: 0 is a valid state. Picking W or the override from the wrong field, or blanket-refusing zero-wage workers, is the plausible fix that is wrong.

The workingYearIrmaaMagiByPerson chain has a writer (questions.tsx forces 0 for retired people) and a backstop gate (simulate's override-required check). Changing the lag-read override needs the full producer, writer, consumer and gate chain traced, not just the two ends.

Workers' taxable wages are a planned stream that a death can cut short. Pricing X over W must use the wages actually realized on the path (a living worker in that year), not the planned working window.

The gross-up's 128-pass cap was proved only inside the declared ENGINE_MAX_* domain. Adding a wage base changes the worst-case tax magnitude, so the eps-bound pass count must be re-derived within that domain.

A new per-year wage/tax-base stream fed into solveGrossWithdrawal needs the same finiteness guard as its sibling streams at validateParams. A NaN slips past ?? and relational checks, runs all 128 passes and throws.

Externally derived fixtures for the incremental working-year tax (§86 provisional income including wages, state tax) must take the rule from the IRS/state worksheet, not the research paraphrase, or the hand math and the engine share one misreading.

solveGrossWithdrawal is unexported and the API returns aggregates only. Clamped-year conversion-tax goldens need the zero-return one-year read-off or the two-run differencing identity, not the engine used as its own oracle.

The plan's enumerated test scenarios (e.g. a crown-moving or override-crossing fixture) are hypotheses. Check with algebra that each mechanism exists in this engine before the plan commits a fixture to it.

The plan was deepened and reviewed. Closing the review loop needs a judgment about the class of remaining findings, not a zero count, and each confirmed prescription needs checking against source before folding. The §7 clamp's missing death term was a round-6 P1 found exactly this way.

Taxing working-year conversions overturns the 'work years carry no tax' premise that other docs cite (e.g. the dip/monotonicity rationale). Grep the whole doc set for premise phrases, not only the files the plan edits.

Adding base B under P changes solveGrossWithdrawal's contraction map; a convergence probe at large net samples the cheap regime, so GROSS_UP_MAX_PASSES must be re-probed at small net and large SS before it is trusted.

The base stacks ordinary income under P and moves which bracket and cap-gains breakpoint P straddles. Re-derive k from the channel sum and prove the worst corner is still disjoint, or the fixed point can silently stop contracting.

The 128-pass closure rests on the eps-bound inside ENGINE_MAX_DOLLAR. A gate-valid huge base raises the tax scale the pass count depends on, so the worst case must be re-derived inside the declared domain.
The floor rides cashTermsForYear's section 7 clamp, which keys income-blind (alive && t < retire). Keying the floor or its reach qualifier on earnedIncomeReal > 0 leaves zero-income workers unpriced.
Byte-identity and reduce-to-spine tests on fixtures whose working-year base is structurally zero pass for any floor bug. At least one fixture must drive a nonzero B and assert the moved value.
solveGrossWithdrawal and GrossUpContext are internal. Externally derived goldens for the floor need the one-year zero-return read-off or the differencing identity, never the engine as its own oracle.

The three-arm max over investment-income readings is a rule selection. Fixture parameters must be walked through which arm wins (and through bracket and phase-out edges) before a hand panel's unanimous arithmetic is trusted.

Goldens for T(base+P,ss) - T(base,ss) + T(0,ss) drawn from our own spec or research paraphrase are one witness, not two. Take the rule (SS inclusion, senior bonus per person, state treatment) from the IRS and state forms.

Nominal-frozen figures in T (the section 86 thresholds, the NC deduction) must deflate by calendar year. A min-cap binds only when it is the smaller arm. The dip re-tune must record the move at the old inputs first and only then re-tune.

The dip seed's non-monotonic curve rests on the section 7 work-year money gradient plus a dual-clock tent. Taxing working years shrinks that gradient, so re-tune from the mechanism, not by knob-twiddling.

The new methodology disclosure row in assumptionRegistry.ts and the v12 ledger text describe engine behaviour. Grep that the engine actually consumes what each sentence claims (state channel, which years, which incomes) before shipping it.
A reach qualifier in stalenessExposure.ts suppresses the pricing-change note. Check it in the silencing direction: a household whose priced working years moved must never read as not reached.

Working years depend on the crown on the date route (buildCandidateParams moves the retirement offset). A reach or disclosure predicate read off the base overlay or the draft diverges from the run the surface describes.

Pricing working-year tax changes the precondition that clamp years carry no withdrawal tax. Re-audit every path that relied on it (bridge or IRMAA override years, windowGate ACA pricing, date candidates).

The year's base B in the clamp is a planned working stream that a death can cut short mid-window. The seam must realize it against the path (a dead worker's base and the filing flip), not carry the plan verbatim.
The floor switches off at the retirement year, and the brackets shift at the MFJ-to-single survivor flip. Test the crossing years, not only static all-working or all-retired fixtures.
Each year's base and SS must be read in that year's own frame. A constant-income witness world cannot catch year-0 income leaking into later years' floor.
A NaN base passes every relational guard and makes the gross-up's convergence test false forever. Gate Number.isFinite first on the new GrossUpContext input.
A new per-year base or investment-income stream threaded into the overlay must mirror its siblings' R19 validation in validateParams; a ?? default does not stop NaN.
Any new fail-loud throw the floor adds in taxOverlay or stateTax narrows what the engine accepts. Sweep validateParams' admission predicate so the case returns indeterminate instead of crashing.
The reduce-to-spine and byte-identity guards must compare every ranked or tax-aware vector, not a total. A floor that reallocates tax between buckets conserves the sum and passes.
When the engine's floor disagrees with a hand ledger, trace the divergent mechanism before patching either side; prefer fixture worlds (r = 0) that make the closed form exact.

The methodology row must not claim a net direction (for example 'makes working longer look worse') for a modelling choice that reaches both arms of a comparison. Disclose the arm-level consequence, hedged.
The gross-up bound (k, 128 passes) is copied across glossary, architecture and plan docs. If the floor changes k, every copy goes stale unless it is replaced with a pointer or gated.
Large edits to taxOverlay.ts and simulate.ts shift the line counts that many doc citations point at. The structural doc-stats gate stays green while the meaning rots, so run doc:reanchor last.
devSeeds.ts is one of the repo's CRLF files. A whole-file rewrite while re-tuning the dip seed flips its EOL and buries the real knob edits in an unreviewable diff.
The real-solve witnesses in devSeeds.test get slower with an extra tax channel. Set their timeouts from a measured isolated run, and do not take green-when-filtered as a green suite.

The §7 working-year clamp fires on an income-blind predicate (alive && t < retire), but its guards were keyed on earnedIncomeReal > 0. A take-home vs spending measurement or a gap filing that only looks at salaried date seeds misses the zero- or low-income worker subdomain, where the clamp still zeroes draws.

cashTermsForYear is the seam where a planned input (retire age, contribution stream) has to be realized against the path's death timeline. The longevity sampler never draws a death before age 66, so a survivor-shortfall claim built on earlier deaths describes paths the engine never produces. That is the exact bullet the commits corrected.

Sourcing FICA for a real-dollar engine: the Additional Medicare Tax thresholds ($200k/$250k) are frozen nominal, and this lesson names 'the Medicare surtax lines' as figures that must divide by cumulativePriceIndex. The SS wage base is indexed by statute, so 'does the statute index it, and in which frame?' decides each figure. Also measure the binding arm of any min/cap before predicting 'no change'.

Take the payroll-tax rule from the primary (the statute, Form 8959, SSA's wage-base notice), never from a research paraphrase. The 'per what' question bites here: the wage-base cap applies per earner, not per household, and fixtures derived from the same paraphrase count as only one witness.

The §7 clamp already carried a missed death term once (a surviving retiree's draws got zeroed). Re-check the clamp's death and survivor arms when measuring per working year, and judge a council or review loop on finding class, not on its count.

The clamp is the dominant work-year gradient on the date sweep (about spend + contributions + avoided premium per work year), so any contribute-and-draw double count inflates every extra work year. On the date seeds that pushes the date early, in the optimistic direction.

FICA figures come from different instruments: the wage base from SSA's annual COLA notice, the 6.2%/1.45%/0.9% rates and the $200k/$250k thresholds from statute. Citing them all to one source asserts a provenance some fields don't have, so cite each figure separately.

Earned income or contributions collapsed to a household scalar can't support a per-earner FICA wage-base cap or a per-person dead-slot check. Keep per-person attribution through the wire and sum at the last consumer.

Take-home vs spending 'per working year' has to judge each year in its own frame, with that year's income and that year's spending. Date seeds that hold income constant across work years cannot show a year where one spouse retires early or a claim starts.

Before filing the contribute-and-draw double count, or any of the 48 audit gaps, as a real hazard, derive that the mechanism exists in this engine (for example, contributions entering at full basis, or the one-continuous-stream structure). A premise-false scenario, like the survivor bullet, reads exactly like a real one.

The work files many register prescriptions from a measurement on a few date seeds. A prescription is a prediction about code nobody ran, and a claim found on one seed but worded for all households is how wrong entries pick up authority over time.

The §7 clamp's working-year predicate is income-blind (alive && t < retire), but the guards are keyed on earnedIncomeReal > 0. A pay check keyed on pay > 0 would miss zero-income workers inside the clamp's domain. Diff the pay check's trigger against the clamp's own predicate, clause by clause.

This exact unit's survivor-shortfall headline (~$33,197 / ~$15,372) was taken over deaths the engine never draws. Any plan figure for the pay check (shortfall, reach, N of 10) must be filtered to reachable rows first, then summarized.

The pay check is D7's remedy for the 'doesn't check your pay covers it' row. The plan must USE the pay and spending the household gave, or ASK for W, never add another disclosure. The stopgap note must stay until this build lands and be retired with it.

The tax floor's 'no reach' claim skipped the Medicare draw (fundingNet) and Social Security's IRMAA-MAGI read. The pay check's reach must count every dollar the portfolio funds and every MAGI look-back, not just the channels it was designed for.

The working-year tax floor's plan named the wrong 'ordinary-wins' witness (dip I=$10,000). Derive which arm wins before naming any pay-check witness, pin the name with its figure, and predict which arms cannot red before planting mutants.

Payroll constants mix indexing rules: the SS wage base and earnings-test limits index by law, while the Additional Medicare Tax lines are frozen nominal (named here as must divide by cumulativePriceIndex). Leaving a frozen line flat-real indexes it, the rosy way.

FICA and earnings-test fixtures that take their RULE from our research paraphrase are one witness, not two. Source the rule from SSA's or the IRS's own form or worksheet (per person vs household, the $1-per-$2 vs FRA-year $1-per-$3 arms).

A new numeric input (W, per-year pay or FICA streams) added beside validated siblings is exactly where validateParams grows a hole. Mirror the siblings' finiteness guards, and never use `?? default` on a field that can be NaN.
Any tolerance or range check on W or the pay shortfall, such as a pay-covers-cost comparison, admits NaN because every comparison with NaN is false. Gate on Number.isFinite first.

Any new fail-loud throw in the pay-check or earnings-test path narrows what the engine accepts. Re-audit validateParams' admission predicate in the same unit so a gate-valid input never crashes mid-path.
A new W or pay dollar input needs the ENGINE_MAX_DOLLAR magnitude bound at the R19 gate. Finiteness alone does not bound compounding or the gross-up's convergence story.

The new confirm-or-correct W answer is persisted, so the restore codec is its sole range gate on the restore path. Finiteness-only lets a finite out-of-range value through. Test a finite out-of-range W, not just NaN.

The §7 clamp once had no death term, so a survivor's draws were zeroed (a P1 found late in a plan-review loop). Deepening this plan needs class-based closure, and each confirmed prescription must be verified against source before folding.

Pay is a plan that the death timeline can cut short inside cashTermsForYear. A dead worker earns nothing and owes no FICA, and the earnings test applies only to living claimants. The seam must realize pay against the path, and fixtures must drive a death inside the working window.

The pay check's thresholds move with evolving state: the retire year, a death mid-window, the FRA year where the earnings test switches regimes. Test each crossing year, not just static working or retired positions.

Pay-check witnesses with constant pay and no mid-window SS claim can't see per-year frame errors such as the earnings test or SS starting during work years. Vary the spanned axis in at least one witness.
Cite FICA and earnings-test figures per FIGURE (wage base, 0.9% thresholds, the two exempt amounts each from its own instrument). Watch for formula figures with a frozen base.

Hand and panel derivations for pay-check fixtures can silently cross a rule boundary (wage-base cap, Additional Medicare threshold, under-FRA vs FRA-year earnings test). Walk each fixture through the selection predicates before pinning.

The FICA wage base and the earnings test are per-PERSON. Collapsing pay to a household scalar early destroys the attribution that the cap, the dead-slot guard and the earnings test need. Carry it per person and sum late.

A new pure earnings-test function in the SS sub-engine must range-guard its own inputs (finite non-negative earnings, a claim age or FRA window). Don't defer that to validateParams, or extrapolation yields a negative withheld benefit or NaN.

The date sweep is monotone partly because the §7 clamp zeroes working-year withdrawals, giving a ~2:1 work-year gradient. A pay check that lets working years draw changes that gradient, and the tuned dip seed's mechanism, on the date route.

On the date route, the per-candidate transform touches accumulation and working-year streams. Any pay-check predicate or disclosure must read the crowned candidate's params, never buildDateInput's base overlay.

Presence-keyed overlays: buildOverlay has a degenerate early return ($0 accounts, no income), so a pay check gated on overlay presence can be silently absent. Mirrors must read the builder's OUTPUT, not re-derive its inputs.

D7's 'use the pay' rule can collide with the reduce-to-spine byte-identity law on households that entered pay but have no overlay. Scope the identity claim, resolve by error direction, and pin both sides.
Every existing working-year fixture has a structurally zero draw (pay covers spending), so equality assertions on the shortfall draw are vacuous. Drive a nonzero W − net-pay shortfall and assert it.

The working-year shortfall draw is internal to an aggregate-only API. Use the zero-return one-year read-off (terminal = P − draw) or a differencing pair to pin it externally instead of using the engine as its own oracle.

The plan's enumerated pay-check scenarios (survivor shortfall, date-route shifts, earnings-test arms) are hypotheses. Derive that each mechanism actually occurs in this engine before writing its fixture into the plan.

The pay check supersedes the premise that the §7 clamp means working years draw nothing. Grep docs, code comments and test rationales (date-sweep monotonicity, the IRMAA override, windowGate) for that premise's wording, not just the new unit's file list.

If the confirmed W is derived from spending, budget lines, OOP medical or contributions, every writer of those inputs must re-reconcile W or flag it stale. Fencing only the new W question leaves the other writers able to break the invariant.

Same module: editing squeaky-clean's SKILL.md contract can quietly weaken its peer-safe rules (commit --only with :(literal) pathspecs, never delete index.lock, no kills while the registry shows other live sessions). A handoff step that tells a peer session apart must use the session registry, because subagent and workflow transcripts carry the parent's session id.

Mutation testing on squeaky-clean plants mutants in SKILL.md too, so a mutant run against the live junction (or a review reading it) reads mutants. Review rounds on this unit stopped converging because each round's fixes opened new seams, so gate on harm class instead of 'until nothing material'.

A cross-session handoff rests on claims about Claude Code's messaging (session naming, delivery, whether the other side can reply). Those claims are maps until a real run measures them, so the SKILL.md contract and docs.test.mjs could encode reasoned-but-unrun platform behavior.

docs.test.mjs pins SKILL.md prose that a later session acts on. The handoff step is rarely-run advice, so its test may only lock in the author's belief. Assert the property the instruction must hold (right recipient, right direction), not just its words.

Q8 lives in the same projects/hooks/probes and run.mjs. Calling the --bg arm VERIFIED on 2.1.309 from reasoning or docs, without a run, or without tying the verdict to its def/lib/capture bytes, repeats the CreationDate and Q6 mistakes. A surprising arm needs its permission_denials and modelUsage read before anyone blames the CLI.

Adding --target claude-json to U3's settings writer adds new write and rollback states. The way-back advice could then name the wrong file or version, or say nothing was written after a write landed, and a test would pin that advice green. Any printed command has to be run in pwsh and sh, and the never-point-back invariant has to be asserted over deploy/rollback sequences.

The --bg arm and throwaway sessions spawn background sessions. A measured label (status values, a notice waking a session) has to cite the run that measured that exact thing, not a neighbouring background-shell measurement. Cleanup also has to account for every writer still running, such as background jobs and Stop hooks, before reporting done.

run.mjs cleanupTargets and the bgJob teardown kill or delete things on a machine where peer sessions run. Killing by name, or deleting from the shared scratch folder without proving each target was spawned by this probe, reaches other sessions' work.

Valuing lineups against an empty slot or unforced starters turns marginal value back into raw points. The trade's lineup delta needs the drop/FA-fill replacement as its counterfactual, and the evaluator should print the lineups it built, not just the score.

A player-value ranking answers a different question from 'what does this roster gain'. Trade value has to be the optimal-lineup delta, ideally through the shared lineup_value.py math. A candidate window that leaves out K/DEF can empty the FA-fill set.

Rosters and projections from api.sleeper.app sit behind Cloudflare stale-while-revalidate, so an on-demand evaluator fetching without a nonce can value a trade against stale rosters that pass every structural check. Route the fetches through the per-call busted fetch.

Joining the three consensus sources to Sleeper players by a name token inside a (team, pos) bucket can return exactly one candidate who is a teammate. Join on player_id or corroborate against an immutable key before treating a match as identity.
Fuzzy name similarity cannot separate same-man from different-man renderings, so a consensus join across external projection sources must not lean on a similarity threshold. Use stable ids.

A projection that failed to join, or a source missing a player, can come through as 0 points. It then reads as a lopsided-trade finding instead of 'could not evaluate'. Run a known-positive check on the join and flag zeros.

A new Python script on this Windows laptop defaults file reads and stdout to cp1252. Arrows or non-ASCII names in the trade report will crash it unless every open() sets encoding='utf-8' and stdout is reconfigured.

The newest file is the one most likely to miss the project's 'always reconfigure stdout to UTF-8' rule. trade_eval.py is new, and its report quotes player names, so it can die while printing the very thing it found.

Green tests don't show that the output gives Briggsy enough to decide on a trade. Write one real evaluation from the tool's output, the way he would read it, to see whether the why, the lineup changes and the counter terms are actually on screen.

How permission rules match is a platform claim: Skill denials in parameter form, Bash vs PowerShell force-push patterns, and deny over ask. If U4 writes these from docs or reasoning without a probe, it can ship rules that look like they block and don't. Each rule needs a run that measures it, read through the run's permission_denials.

U4's TODO and private plan record answers Briggsy still owes (D3, the landing consent). The trap is writing 'settled' or 'consented' before his words are on a line. Write 'asked' or 'owed' until they land, and say plainly when he handed the call to the pilot.

A deny/ask rule is a text pattern, so it is a claim about every string it matches. A loose one over-matches: denying 'gemini' would also catch gemini-grounding, the research agents' web search. It can also miss forms like -f, +refspec and --force-with-lease. Check each pattern against every command form it could meet.

The settings-writer tests touch a home-relative config path. If a test builds its fixture path with the code's own settings-path helper, a mutant of that helper can write the real ~/.claude/settings.json. Build fixture paths from the test's own root, and diff the real file around mutation runs.

U4 lands its permissions through U3's settings writer, whose way-back advice and rollback are the least-run code. A half-failed permissions write needs advice that never points back at the state being escaped, and every printed command has to run in both pwsh and sh.

matchesPush/pushesByStructure decide on command text, so a loose pattern catches every command that merely contains the phrase. The work's own landmine is the example: a commit message that quotes a force push would be refused. Check the matcher against every shape the text can take, not just the one push you have in mind.

The allow-rule reader and the plugin-grants logic are a model of how Claude Code matches permission rules. Each rule stays a map until Q17/Q18 actually measure it. A verdict holds only for the bytes it was read from, so stopping the probe reruns after CLI updates means saying which verdicts are now stale.

The commits write TODO, memory and flight-plan records about what is decided and what is built (D3 flips ask to deny, 'decided, not built'; 'Briggsy approved'; the cut is built). Each line must state its real state and point to the words or code behind it, never a hopeful 'built' or 'confirmed'.

This is round 2 of a review-and-fix loop on a safety unit that guesses intent from command structure, and round 3 is queued. Round-2 fixes to the push matcher can open round 3's seams. Count the findings that trace back to prior fixes, and gate the landing on harm class, not 'nothing material'; the scope cut is that structural move.

Q17/Q18 run in the probes' trusted folder, and the permissions and plugin-grants readers resolve real config locations. Build test fixture paths from the test's own root, never from the code under test, and diff the real roots around any mutation run so a mutant can't touch real settings or the temp folder.

In survivorBenefitAnnual, the at/after-survivor-FRA early return skipped the only applyFactorAnnual guard and so leaked a silent NaN. Reordering RIB-LIM against the age reduction can move or bypass the claim-age guard and evaluate the piecewise factor outside its window.

The survivor base must use the deceased's REALIZED claim age (realizedClaimAgeAtDeath, FRA floor), never the planned one. RIB-LIM keys on the benefit the deceased actually drew, so the fix can read the plan. The hand-derived seam goldens ($19,587.60, own-wins vs survivor-wins) are the ones that need re-deriving.

Goldens for the fixed order must come from the primary rule text (SSA POMS / CFR RIB-LIM computation), not the research paraphrase the wrong order was written from. Independent arithmetic over the same misread rule is one witness, not two.

RIB-LIM is a cap, so the order only changes a result where the cap binds. Measure each seed before predicting 'no seed moves' for the SOLVER_CODE_VERSION call. When a seed's figure moves, record the move at the old inputs in its docblock before re-pinning or re-tuning.

The pricing-ledger row's reach and the bump decision must count every consumer of the survivor benefit: the survivor floor, provisional income under §86, IRMAA MAGI two years on, and the step-down readout. Counting only the survivor stream is the miss this lesson documents.

Survivor fixtures built with pia=0 structurally zero the §202 survivor benefit, so they cannot discriminate the order. The step-down golden ($1,000/mo, survivor drawing at age 60) is a downstream pin the fix can move.

Walk each re-pinned fixture through the rule's conditions: RIB-LIM applies only when the deceased filed early, and the reduction only when the survivor claims before survivor FRA. Otherwise unanimous hand math confirms the wrong rule.
Goldens where RIB-LIM does not bind, or where the survivor claims at FRA, give the same value under both orders. A wrong-order regression would pass them. At least one pin must sit where both apply.
When the re-pinned engine figure and a hand derivation disagree, trace the mechanism first. Never re-pin the goldens by copying the new engine output (engine-as-oracle).
Hand-derived Social Security figures must honor SSA's monthly dime-floor rounding. Where rounding falls relative to the reduction and the limit can shift re-pinned goldens by cents.

Any measured impact quoted for the bump decision must be filtered to deaths the engine actually draws (none before 65) before taking magnitudes. Otherwise the headline describes deaths that never occur.

Choosing not to bump SOLVER_CODE_VERSION is the silencing direction: saved recommendations priced under the old order would be re-presented as current. Judge the stamp by whether the solves it dates change, not by the stamp itself.
The filed order-fix prescription does not inherit trust from its diagnosis. Verify the prescribed order and the named mechanism against source and POMS before executing it.

The working-year clamp keys income-blind (alive && t < retire) while its guards keyed on earnedIncomeReal > 0. U5's required schedule, stream and survivor W in that same clamped block can key on a proxy like pay > 0 instead of the clamp's own predicate, which leaves zero-pay workers unguarded.

A change to the working-year base reaches every dollar the portfolio funds (fundingNet, the Medicare draw) and every MAGI read (SS on provisional income, the IRMAA look-back). The dateSearch reach walk and the floor-to-fundingNet composition undercount if they list only the feature's own channels.

Reading the earnings-test schedule in every year means judging each year by its own lines AND its own income. A year-0 skeleton, or witnesses whose income never changes from year to year, hides a mixed-frame error.

Survivor W, own deposits and the stream are plans the death timeline can cut short. The seam must stop the dead worker's pay and deposits at death, and fixtures must drive a death-before-retirement path, not only the case where the plan plays out as written.

The pay check's own survivor-shortfall headline was taken over deaths the engine never draws (none before 65). Any reach or shortfall figure the check reports for survivor W or the reach walk must filter to reachable deaths before taking the max.

Survivor W and the earnings test move the required amount at the death year and the FRA year. Static couple-only or survivor-only fixtures cannot prove the clamped block switches correctly in the year the change happens.

The shortfall stream is zero on almost every seed because pay covers what is required, so byte-exact equality on the stream or the observation hook is vacuous unless one fixture drives a nonzero shortfall.

The date sweep stays monotone because the clamp zeroes working-year withdrawals (the work-year money gradient). U5's stream weakens that gradient, so date-seed crowns, the dip seed and the reach walk's expectations can move.

On the date route the working-year streams depend on the retirement offset and are rebuilt per candidate by buildCandidateParams. A reach walk that reads the base overlay instead of each candidate's params reports the wrong run.

The consumedConstants family rule is an enumeration that defines the run. A newly consumed constant, here the earnings-test schedule read every year, must join it in the same commit or the staleness check silently under-binds.

A consumedConstants entry is a claim about what the engine reads. Grep the actual consumers so the family list neither names constants nothing reads nor misses the earnings-test schedule's new per-year reads.

Earnings-test thresholds are indexed by statute and compared with same-year earnings inside a real-dollar engine. Reading them every year means picking the right price frame (flat-real or deflated), and measuring before predicting 'no change'.

The hoisted working-year floor's witness label was already wrong once (dip I=$10,000 named 'ordinary-wins'). Derive which arm wins before naming the floor-to-fundingNet composition witnesses, and predict each mutant's kill set before running it.

The observation hook must stay observe-only (spine byte-identity) and carry the engine's own decision, such as who is working or a survivor, on the wire, so consumers never re-derive it from ages or other inputs.

The own-deposit helper and survivor W must keep per-person attribution through to the overlay, so the dead-slot guard can vet a dead spouse's pay and deposits. Collapsing them early into a household total leaves only bad guard choices.

Building year 0 by calling the run's own functions on the same inputs is still a re-derivation. It forks wherever the overlay has an early return or guard (no overlay, degenerate household) that the ledger doesn't replay. The cross-check against the overlay's recorded year 0 has to be what proves the two agree, and it should be seen going red under a planted fork.

Naming Medicare onset or charges from ages (currentAge + t >= 65) re-derives an engine decision. The engine's onset is max(65 - age, retireOffset), so a spouse still working past 65 isn't enrolled, and that is exactly the working-year household. Read the run's own enrollment count and medicareChargeForYear, never an age proxy.

Naming every later working year that changes or runs short means judging each year in its own frame: that year's claims, earnings-test step, Medicare, NC rate and bonus. Extending a year-0 skeleton across years is the mixed-frame bug. A witness with constant income can't catch it, so vary income across years in at least one fixture.

If the cross-check against the overlay's year 0 (or the largest-remainder sum check) compares only totals, it passes any shift of dollars between lines. Compare every line, and pair it with a witness showing a planted reallocation goes red.

The year-0 cross-check is an equality assertion. On fixtures where Medicare, state tax, SS or catch-up lines are structurally $0, both sides read 0 and a zeroed or swapped line passes. Drive each line to a non-zero value that differs from its neighbours.

The import-allowlist source test can be bypassed by dynamic import(), export-from re-exports, .mts/.cts files, deep subpaths, and imports spread over several lines. Probe it with planted versions of each bypass so it isn't only green on the easy cases.

Naming a senior-bonus sunset (or an NC rate step) as a change has to come from the run's computed value actually moving, not from sunsetAfter metadata. Otherwise the ledger reports a loss for a household that never got the bonus (no one 65+, or phased out by MAGI).

The ledger must read the producer of the run it describes. On the date route the crowned candidate's transform window-gates healthcare and onsets, so reading the base overlay for a W-present run describes a different run.

A diagnostic built on a reference path (the bare helpers) can disagree with the shipped decision path (the overlay's real fixed point and floor) while looking confident. Compose through the shipped path and pin the two together.

Year labels on later events: a flow (pay, tax, a Medicare bill) belongs to sim-year t and calendar year start + t. Mixing a readout row's end-of-year index with sim-year offsets puts claims, onset or NC steps one year off with nothing to show it.

The money picture's lines must cover every dollar the portfolio funds in a working year (the Medicare draw) and every read of that year's income (SS into provisional and IRMAA-MAGI). Listing only the feature's own nouns leaves a line out.

This is the same pay-check feature. Runs-short years and worst-shortfall figures must be computed only on reachable timelines (no deaths before 65 that the engine never draws), filtered first, not caveated afterwards in prose.

Every later-year event (claim, earnings-test step, Medicare onset, catch-up step-down, NC step, sunset) is a state-driven crossing. Test the crossing year itself, not only static positions on either side.
A per-year mapping pinned only by year 0 or by equal-valued years lets a year-0-constant or wrong-offset mutant pass. Fixtures need distinct values in later years.
Which years count as working years has to use the working-year clamp's own predicate (alive and t < retire), not a proxy like earned > 0, or zero-income workers fall outside the ledger.

When the composed year 0 and the overlay's recorded year 0 disagree, trace why before loosening a tolerance or patching either side. The size and sign of the difference point at the mechanism that was left out.

A cross-check of the ledger against the overlay is two engine paths sharing the same functions: one witness counted twice. It proves the plumbing, not the tax or SS rule, so the goldens still need an outside source.

The working-year tax floor's own witness label was wrong (the ordinary-wins arm). Work out which arm wins before naming a witness for prepareWorkingYearFloor, and write down which tests each mutant should red before running it.

Any new fail-loud throw in the producer (a cross-check mismatch, an unexpected regime) narrows what the engine accepts. Re-check that validateParams still refuses calmly everything that now reaches the throw.
A source-text import test built on a first-match regex can match an import inside a comment or miss one written oddly. Strip comments and anchor on real import statements, and run a negative control.
Assert the import allowlist as an exact set. A contains or subset check stays green when an extra, forbidden import is added.
After largest-remainder rounding, a runs-short or changes decision keyed on raw dollars can name a year whose rounded line reads $0. Key the claim on the quantity that is actually shown.

gameday_check.score silently drops stat keys it does not know (Sleeper's fgm_50p / fgmiss_<range> vs the league's fgm_50_59 / fgmiss), so every kicker scores low. The work could carry that into projected_total and the Expected header, and the header would still look like a clean number. Sleeper-only magnitude is the other trap, since a three-site projection can flip the sign.

A cached feed can return data that is well-formed, authentic, and old. Live points from api.sleeper.app (Cloudflare, stale-while-revalidate) or a cached ESPN scoreboard can show a game as scheduled after kickoff, or show old point totals, and every shape check still passes. Each fetch needs a nonce that is unique per call, plus a freshness check, applied to every endpoint on that host.

A broken instrument returns zero, and zero reads like a finding. If the live-points join or the stat-key mapping misses, an in-progress or finished player reads 0, which looks like "hasn't scored yet." Run a positive control on a player known to have scored before trusting the live column.

Guard the number together with its label. Printing a pregame projected_total under "Expected" after games have started, or a live-plus-remaining figure under a label that implies something else, makes a correct number tell a lie. No check reads the label.

Joining players to ESPN scoreboard games by team code (Sleeper WAS vs ESPN WSH, bye weeks) can find no game. That miss must print as unverified. It must never be silently read as "not started, add the full projection" or "final, add nothing." "I could not check" must never print like "I checked."

Tests confirm the code does what it was written to do, not that the header gives Briggsy what he needs on game day. Compose a real Expected header from live data, mid-game and at final, and read it. Any fact you have to fetch from somewhere else is a finding.

The exact defect: a region above the controls resizes on a blur-commit, so the tap lands one control off. Only coordinate input in a real browser sees it, and the cure has to hold for both a thumb (blur on touch) and a mouse.

A blur-commit and the following click can run in one task with no re-render between them. If the hold's freeze/release reads state captured at render time, it acts on a world one commit old, and touch's mouse events after touchend change when blur fires relative to click.

On the 1024x1366 touch arm, a synthetic tap at an element's exact edge can send no pointerdown to it, so the hold never arms and the arm reads red or green for the wrong reason. Inset every coordinate tap by at least 1px.

'Mutant-proven' arms: plant exactly the named regression (the hold removed), and write down beforehand which arms must go red and which cannot (the mouse arm vs the touch arm, the 1536 vs 1024 tiers), or a too-broad plant over-kills and the proof is mislabeled.

Same face (WorkingCostQuestion, the period tap). A hold set at pointerdown has to be dropped on every exit: pointercancel, pointerup off target, no click, unmount. Otherwise it is a mark with a setter and no dropper, and the stale note stays frozen out of view.

The other cure for the same shift is to reserve the above-control box by stacking the real alternatives hidden, never a guessed em reserve. Weigh it against the gesture hold before committing to a timing-based fix.

A new verify:fit arm that waits on an absence (no shift, no note) passes vacuously before and after the blur-commit. Wait for a state only the commit creates, and prove the wait actually waits, so the tap really races the shift.

The eaten tap depends on geometry that differs between ubuntu CI and Windows text metrics. A mutant-red seen only locally may not reproduce in CI; check that the shift really moves 'Each month' out from under the tap point where the gate runs.
After tapping 'Each month', asserting with a state-dependent locator (e.g. :not(:checked)) re-resolves to another radio. Pin the radio by a value attribute that survives the click.

Playwright's .click() scrolls the target into view and re-resolves its coordinates, which hides the mid-gesture shift. The arms must use raw coordinate gestures a reader could make, and confirm what the gesture actually hit.
1024px sits below the 68rem breakpoint (1088px), so the touch arm renders the stacked tier. Assert which tier rendered before asserting the tap law, so the arm tests the layout it claims to.
If the coordinate-tap arms go in a new e2e spec, the denylist CSP harness adopts it (dev-only seed routes against dist) unless the harness partition names exactly one owner config for it.
